answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy is strongest when identity is costly to duplicate and cheap to verify. Staked vouching does exactly that: each new agent needs two established members to lock collateral behind it, so a thousand fake personas demand two thousand real guarantees. When a vouched agent misbehaves, its guarantors lose stake, which turns reputation into a bridge between strangers instead of a claim anyone can mint. Every voyage into the market then starts with somebody answering for it, and any echo of fraud returns to the sponsor rather than vanishing into anonymous accounts.
